feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain specialization in public-sector platforms, governance, and content operations. It presents solid scope and progression, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary quickly establish a distinctive niche in digital platform leadership, communications systems, and AI-enabled experiences.  
- Strong credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement supports leadership claims and subject-matter depth.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well but not results. Include gains in traffic, engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use parallel punctuation in lists, standardize “organization-wide/organisation-wide” style, and remove comma inconsistency such as “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other lists without the serial comma. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years guiding web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add a proof point from recent roles, e.g. “Led a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace “Leads” with first-person-neutral summary language like “Specializes in” or “Experienced in” for consistency with CV tone.
- Consider trimming “multimedia production” or “AI-enabled user experiences” unless you want those as differentiators in the opening.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of capabilities closely repeats Core Competencies; use the intro for positioning plus 1–2 standout achievements instead.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scanability and reduce repetition.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and remove filler terms like “operations” where possible.
- Reorder for strongest current value: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation, communications, multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, measurement, and reporting • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Consider changing “Enterprise website modernization” to “Enterprise web modernization” for cleaner style and broader scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific language here.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” and “Multi-channel communications operations” partially overlap; consider merging or sharpening the distinction.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more additive and portfolio-like.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise, parallel bullet for easier scanning.
- Replace generic verbs like “Built” and “Developed” with more specific leadership/ownership language: “Led,” “Designed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Add outcome, audience, or scale where possible (for example: user group, campaign purpose, conference/event context, or organizational reach).
- Standardize style: use either sentence fragments or full sentences throughout; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the most recent Work Experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may be the best differentiator if framed as a distinct cross-channel project with unique scope or impact.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant-level scope, recent strategic contributions, and concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Rephrase technical build work to show outcomes: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member toolkits.”
- Add measurable results where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow efficiencies, search improvements, or engagement/performance gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep a brief mention here and let the project section carry the detail.
- “Governance, usability, workflows, analytics” repeats prior NACo roles; frame this item around external advisory scope and new initiatives since Oct. 2024.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize highest-impact wins first: Drupal migration, analytics infrastructure, in-house studio, governance/operations.
- Make channel bullet more outcome-driven: add list growth, engagement, open/click rates, campaign results, or audience size if available; otherwise trim it.
- Tighten phrasing: “Migrated NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a more strategic/organizational level.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries and footer projects; emphasize building the studio and expanding internal production capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function, then focus bullets on distinct contributions: “Ran day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy distribution.”
- Tighten newsletter bullet: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-led: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague bullets with stronger operational language: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program staff” and “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep only if framed as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and governance strengths rather than broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets such as:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for complex public-sector organizations
- Audience-centered content strategy and campaign planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Mission-driven stakeholder communications” if you want a broader, more executive tone.
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid vague terms like “focused” where “audience-centered” or “user-centered” is stronger.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) for recent experience bullets, not skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep this item high-level and distinct.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize platform leadership and recent execution strengths rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they are already covered in Technical + IT.
- Replace “CMS modernization” with a more outcome-oriented phrase like “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large-scale web platform migration.”
- If space allows, align with recent impact: “AI-enabled search and discovery” and “workflow automation” are stronger differentiators than older/general platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” platform and coding lists.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and search optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, content performance and user-behavior analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and Technical + IT more tool-specific.
- “Leadership reporting” is a bit vague; “executive dashboarding” or “decision-support reporting” is sharper.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is generic and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery scope, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event production
- In-house studio buildout and studio operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the Director-level experience.
- Group related items to reduce fragmentation: combine livestreaming + hybrid/virtual events into one line.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale/context instead of tools alone (e.g., “recurring advocacy programming” or “in-house studio operations”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” from Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless balanced with leadership-level phrasing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add level/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migration, custom content structures) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first and keep it**, since it is the clearest recent, high-impact platform in your experience.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just “Power Pages.”
- If space allows elsewhere, add proficiency/context rather than more tools, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration)”—but only if consistent with the format of other Technical + IT items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or using this item for platform names only and the Topline section for broader capabilities.
- **GitHub Pages** may feel lower-signal than your enterprise CMS work unless it supports a specific recent project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, front-end troubleshooting, CMS implementation**
- Drop versioned/basic terms like **HTML5** and **CSS3** unless required by the role; they add little seniority signal.
- If accurate, add outcome-oriented specificity elsewhere in the CV, e.g., **used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, deployment workflows, and lightweight edge/serverless integrations**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already appear in **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping detail in only one place.
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** if primarily used for tagging/measurement rather than implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more senior by grouping tools by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Automation & Workflow Systems:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Put the true automation tools first; they best support your recent leadership narrative around systems, governance, and cross-team operations.
- Standardize naming for polish: use **Microsoft Teams** instead of Teams; consider commas within groups and bullets/separators between groups.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one short impact cue tied to recent work, e.g., “used to streamline editorial planning and cross-department workflows,” rather than adding more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing nearby.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals—grouping them prevents the list from feeling padded.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email platform ownership rather than just tool familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter and member communications systems**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • High-volume newsletter distribution and audience engagement operations**
- Keep only platforms you directly administered or implemented; order by strongest/recentest platform first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating audience-size claims here unless you remove them from experience.
- “Multi-channel communications” is already covered elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills section. In Technical + IT, it should be tighter, more tool-focused, and avoid broad capability terms already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** if that’s the actual platform used; tools are stronger here than broad disciplines.
- Remove **Dashboarding** unless you name the tool only; dashboarding is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently evidenced tools: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • A/B testing**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping strategy/capability language there and making this section tools-only.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader digital strategy language elsewhere and is less specific than the named platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes and less emphasis on responsibilities repeated in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to stress early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and informally guided a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- Consider a sharper full version: “Promoted through two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, streamlined multi-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring livestream and video content for member communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo entries; keep this version more tactical/foundational.
- “weekly video updates” is close to the later advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: audience reached, number of episodes, stakeholder groups served, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider dropping “contributed to” in favor of stronger verbs like “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first-podcast milestone.
- Avoid repeating broad digital operations language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is currently too generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already covered in Core Competencies and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with production capabilities framed consistently.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing/production • Livestream studio operations**
